newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOREST FIRMS' WASTE PAPER USE SEEN RISING.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOREST FIRMS' WASTE PAPER USE SEEN RISING.

text.p: Finnish forest industry firms' use of waste paper as a raw material in paper production is expected to rise to 2.4 million tonnes this year from almost 2.1 million tonnes in 1996, the Forest Industries Federation said on Monday.

"In 1997, use of waste paper by foreign units (of Finnish paper industry groups) will rise to at least 1.8 million tonnes, in which case the total consumption will be about 2.4 million tonnes," the federation said in a statement.
In 1996, collection of waste paper in Finland rose on the previous year, to 563,000 tonnes, it said.

"The paper industry used a total of 584,000 tonnes of waste paper as raw material (in Finland)," it said, adding that units of Finnish forest industry groups abroad used three times that amount and the volume was still rising.
About 60 percent of paper and board consumed in Finland was collected for recycling, the federation said.
"The forest industry invested almost 800 million markka in environmental protection in Finland in 1996," it said.
About 60 percent of environmental protection investment went into developing production processes and 40 percent went into purification equipment, it said.
The industry invested about 510 million markka in water conservation and about 200 million markka in air protection, the federation said.
"Waste water emissions decreased considerably in 1996," it said.
Phosphorus and nitrogen emissions fell about 20 percent, and chlorine compound emissions fell more than 30 percent, the federation said.
